sprint_note: Sprint 07 renames quantity_g to base_quantity across schema, migrations, backend, and frontend. Semantics are unified: base_quantity is always non-null (NOT NULL DEFAULT 100) after migration. Rescale formula simplified from per100g*newQty/100 to perUnit*newQty. No new endpoints; no new columns.
summary: FoodTracker records daily food intake, computes nutritional aggregates, and serves them through a Dataset-based API consumed by the Atlas Shell UI.

classification.why_application: Contains domain-specific meal-logging rules, nutritional scaling logic, and report aggregation that has meaning only within the FoodTracker domain.
non_goals: Changes to the report tab or standards tab
Any UI to distinguish gram-based vs serving-based entries — naming convention is sufficient
Validation that base_quantity is an integer for serving-based entries
Storing per-unit reference values separately in the database
classification.not_platform: Meal logging, nutritional aggregation, and scaling logic encode FoodTracker-specific business rules; they must not become reusable platform capabilities.

provides: GET /api/food/report — Dataset with per-meal-type kcal/protein/alcohol buckets; avg columns when scope in (year, month, week)
GET /api/food/entries — Dataset of food_logs rows (overview schema)
[CHANGED] GET /api/food/entries/:id — EntryDetail JSON (non-Dataset); now returns base_quantity: float (always non-null)
[CHANGED] PUT /api/food/entries/:id — full-replace edit; field renamed to base_quantity; defaults to 100 if absent
[CHANGED] POST /api/food/meals — intake with optional base_quantity scaling; field renamed from quantity_g
[CHANGED] GET /api/food/template — plain-text JSON template updated with base_quantity
invariants: [CHANGED] base_quantity stored in food_logs is always > 0 (NOT NULL, CHECK constraint, DEFAULT 100)
[CHANGED] Legacy rows that had quantity_g=NULL are backfilled to base_quantity=100 by migration
[CHANGED] When base_quantity is present at intake, all stored macro values are base_quantity/100 * per-100g input
Cross-field checks (good_fat_g <= fat_g, red_meat_g <= meat_g) apply to per-100g values before scaling
avg columns (kcal_avg, protein_avg, alcohol_g_avg) are present in rows if and only if scope is year, month, or week
alcohol_g_total included in every report bucket row regardless of scope
Client-side search does not affect backend — GET /api/food/entries response is always unfiltered
failure_modes: [CHANGED] VALIDATION_ERROR (422): base_quantity present but not a number > 0
VALIDATION_ERROR (422): any required nutrition field missing or invalid
NOT_FOUND (404): entry id does not exist
INVALID_PARAM (422): scope or mode not in allowed set

provides: HTTP API at /api/food/* (all routes registered via FastAPI router in backend/main.py)

internal_flow.name: migration_rename_column
internal_flow.description: migrations/006_rename_quantity_g.sql: (1) UPDATE food_logs SET quantity_g=100 WHERE quantity_g IS NULL to backfill legacy NULLs. (2) ALTER TABLE RENAME COLUMN quantity_g TO base_quantity. (3) ALTER COLUMN base_quantity SET NOT NULL, SET DEFAULT 100. (4) DROP CONSTRAINT food_logs_quantity_g_pos. (5) ADD CONSTRAINT food_logs_base_quantity_pos CHECK (base_quantity > 0). Wrapped in BEGIN/COMMIT.

internal_flow.name: schema_sql_update
internal_flow.description: In schema.sql: replace the quantity_g column block and the food_logs_quantity_g_pos constraint with base_quantity NOT NULL DEFAULT 100 and food_logs_base_quantity_pos CHECK (base_quantity > 0). Comment updated to reflect Sprint 07 semantics.

internal_flow.name: intake_base_quantity
internal_flow.description: In food.py _validate_and_normalise: rename quantity_g to base_quantity throughout validation step 9 and normalised output dict. Behavior is unchanged: when base_quantity present and > 0, scale all nutrition.* by base_quantity/100. When absent, default to 100 (no scaling). Update TEMPLATE_JSON: replace quantity_g with base_quantity; update notes field.
outputs: normalised dict with base_quantity key; INSERT column base_quantity

internal_flow.name: intake_db_insert_base_quantity
internal_flow.description: In commit_meal (food.py): replace quantity_g with base_quantity in the INSERT column list and VALUES tuple. base_quantity from normalised dict is always a float (defaulted to 100 when absent).

internal_flow.name: entry_detail_base_quantity
internal_flow.description: In _serialise_entry_detail (entries.py): replace quantity_g serialisation with: 'base_quantity': float(row['base_quantity']). No null check needed — base_quantity is always non-null after migration.

internal_flow.name: entry_edit_base_quantity
internal_flow.description: In _validate_entry_edit_request (entries.py): rename step 10 from quantity_g to base_quantity. Change from optional to required-with-default: if absent from PUT body, default to 100. Validation: must be a number > 0. Validated dict key becomes 'base_quantity' (float). In UPDATE SQL: replace quantity_g = %s with base_quantity = %s.
inputs: PUT body optional base_quantity (number > 0, defaults to 100)

internal_flow.name: copy_entry_base_quantity
internal_flow.description: In copy_entry (entries.py): replace quantity_g in INSERT column list and VALUES; use source['base_quantity'] (always float after migration).

internal_flow.name: frontend_entry_detail_base_quantity
internal_flow.description: In EntryDetailPage.tsx: (1) In EntryDetail interface: replace quantity_g: number | null with base_quantity: number. (2) In EntryFormState: replace quantity_g: number | null with base_quantity: number. (3) In entryToFormState: base_quantity: entry.base_quantity. (4) Rename per100g state to perUnit; change computation from stored*100/quantity_g to stored/base_quantity. (5) Always compute perUnit on load (no null guard). (6) Rename handleQuantityChange to handleBaseQuantityChange; change rescale formula from perUnit[f]*newQty/100 to perUnit[f]*newQty. (7) Remove the null guard around the quantity field display — always show 'Base quantity' input. (8) In _buildPutBody: replace quantity_g with base_quantity.
outputs: Macro fields updated proportionally in form state
PUT body includes base_quantity and rescaled macros

forbidden: New platform packages for nutritional logic
Storing per-unit reference values as separate columns
A type flag or separate column to distinguish gram-based from serving-based entries

risks.impact: If backend restarts before migration runs, all food_logs writes fail. Migration must be applied first.
